Subject: Unexpected Q3 burst — reconciliation ask

Hi Soojin,

Quick note from our side as we prepare the renewal paperwork: our finance team found a ~44% spike in inference hours for a two‑week window in August that wasn’t in our forecast. We ran the usage_report_q3.csv (attached) and it looks like a legacy job that reprocessed old assets kicked off and consumed a lot of capacity.

Is there a recommended path on your side for reconciling retroactive usage? We are open to a one‑time top‑up or an amortized credit against the renewal, but we need the final numbers by next Friday to avoid delaying Procurement.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Data Platform | Painterly Inc.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Unexpected Q3 burst — reconciliation ask

Elena — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the CSV. I reviewed the file and can confirm the spike matches a reprocess job that ran on Redwood's legacy ingestion cluster before your current batching rules were applied.

Options we typically offer in these situations (happy to go through numbers live):
- One‑time usage settlement: bill the excess hours at your committed rate, with a goodwill credit applied to the renewal invoice (we can offer up to 25% credit for the surge window depending on terms).
- Amortized option: convert the one‑time charge into a three‑month amortized top‑up applied as a fixed capacity addendum to the renewal.
- Waive and extend: if Painterly expands committed capacity by >=20% with a 12‑month extension, we can waive the excess charge entirely and include a partial onboarding credit.

I’m looping Ben for the precise math and Karthik from Finance/Legal for amendment language. Could you confirm which option Procurement would prefer by Monday so we can produce a draft amendment?

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Manager | Redwood Inference

Team / Painterly — did a quick calc against Painterly's committed rate and the usage file. Key points:
- Excess inference hours in spike window: 142,400 token‑hours equivalent.
- Committed rate (per agreed SKU): $0.026 / token‑hour.
- One‑time gross = $3,702.40.
- Proposed customer credit (goodwill) = 20% => net one‑time charge = $2,961.92.
- Amortized option (3 months) => $987.31 / month added to renewal invoices.

Elena — procurement preference will drive wording but either of the above can be captured in a short amendment: 1) one‑time settlement invoice and renewal credit schedule, or 2) capacity addendum with amortized charge and effective date aligned to the renewal.

I attached a proposed_amendment_draft.docx (internal draft) to this thread. If Painterly wants option (3) waive+expand we’ll need an LOI to lock the 12‑month extension.

Ben Carter
